published.title: The Empty Chair
published.body:
Every Sunday, an elderly woman named Margaret sat in the same pew at church. Beside her was an empty chair.

For years, her husband had occupied that seat. After he passed away, she continued saving it.

One morning, a young man entered the church looking defeated. He stood near the entrance, unsure where to sit.

Margaret noticed him and smiled.

"There's a place right here," she said, pointing to the empty chair.

The young man sat beside her.

After the service, he admitted that he had almost given up on life. He had walked into the church hoping to find a reason to keep going.

Margaret gently took his hand.

"Sometimes God leaves a space in our lives because someone else is going to need it."

That Sunday, the chair wasn't empty anymore.

And neither was Margaret's heart.

published.title: The Weight We Carry
published.body:
A man walked along a quiet road carrying a heavy backpack filled with stones.

Every stone represented something he refused to release.

One was regret.

Another was anger.

Others carried the names of people who had hurt him.

As the miles passed, his shoulders grew tired and his steps became slower.

Eventually, he stopped beside a river.

He opened the backpack and examined each stone.

For the first time, he asked himself why he was still carrying things that belonged to yesterday.

One by one, he placed the stones beside the water.

He couldn't change what had happened.

He couldn't rewrite the past.

But he could decide what he carried into tomorrow.

When he stood again, the road hadn't changed.

The distance ahead was still the same.

But his journey had become lighter.

Sometimes healing begins when we finally put something down.

published.title: The Light in the Window
published.body:
Every evening, a little girl watched her father turn on the porch light.

"Why do you leave it on all night?" she asked.

Her father smiled.

"So anyone trying to find their way home can see where they're going."

Years passed, and the little girl grew older.

Eventually, she moved away and experienced the difficulties of adulthood.

There were moments when life felt overwhelming and she wondered whether she had lost her way.

One evening, after a particularly difficult day, she returned to her childhood home.

As she turned onto the familiar street, she noticed something.

The porch light was still shining.

Her father was waiting at the door.

She realized that the light had never been about electricity.

It was about love.

It was about hope.

It was about knowing that no matter how dark the journey became, there was still somewhere she belonged.

And perhaps that's what faith is.

A light that remains on, even when we cannot see the road.
